findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: No step makes the change description name the root cause, which acceptance bullet 1 requires
findings.evidence: The request's first acceptance bullet: 'The root cause is named in the change description'. Decision 4 says the change description marks the facts-file edit as forced. Steps 4 and 5 put the root cause in D189 and CHANGELOG.md. No step tells the producer to state the root cause, and why the fix addresses it, in its change description/report, and the criterion-1 demonstration reads only the CHANGELOG.md and decisions diffs. Fix: Add to step 6 (or a new step) that the producer's change description states the root cause (the producer brief had no guidance for flaky or racy failures), the failure class and the four jobs, and why the paragraph prevents the class. Have the criterion-1 demonstration check the change description too.

findings.summary: The shell-loop anchor is a denylist of six program names and misses other loop-capable programs
findings.evidence: The test asserts that the producer command keys contain none of for, while, until, seq, sh or bash. If the list gained a looping or exec-capable program such as xargs, env, timeout, python or perl, the prompt's 'the Bash policy denies shell loops' would become false and the test would still pass. Today the keys are cargo, git, ls, rm, mv and chmod (athena.toml:84). Fix: Either widen the denylist to the common loop and exec programs (xargs, env, timeout, watch, python, perl, sh, bash, zsh, seq), or assert the keys are a subset of an allow-set, with a message that says to recheck the prompt sentence when a program is added. Note the tradeoff in D189.

findings.summary: The design-stage gap named by the failure class ('…supplies-design') is deferred, not fixed
findings.evidence: The failure class says the person running Athena had to supply the design, and design comes from the planner. The planner frame (crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md) has about 95 tokens of room (planner 1105 of 1200), and the request's Files line is 'crates/'. The accepted reading lists only the producer prompt, so the plan names the gap and proposes the fix, which the root-cause default allows. Fix: Keep the deferral but make it concrete: put the exact proposed planner sentence in D189 and the CHANGELOG entry so a follow-up job can lift it as written. Optionally raise it as an open question for the user, since the room exists.
findings.location: Decision 7; Risks (planner can still hand the producer a call-site plan)

findings.summary: Pinning 'exactly one paragraph follows' makes the prompt rigid for unrelated future edits
findings.evidence: The test asserts that exactly one paragraph follows the guidance and that it starts 'Before you report…'. Any later prose added after the guidance for an unrelated reason would fail this flaky-test guidance test, with a misleading message. Fix: Assert only that the last paragraph starts 'Before you report, reread…' and that the guidance paragraph comes before it. Or word the failure message so it says the report step must stay last.

summary: I read the plan against the snapshot, and the round-3 plan is sound. The files and functions it names exist: producer.md is one paragraph on line 3, which ends with the "Before you report…" sentence. In lib.rs, include_str! is at :21, producer_section at :51, producer_grant at :59-69, the tests module at :118 and the JobConfig pattern at :141/:158. producer_commands is a BTreeMap, and athena.toml:84/:117 list only cargo, git, ls, rm, mv and chmod. policy.rs:6-10 splits commands at ; and newlines and checks each program against that list, so a for or seq loop is denied, as the plan says. stand_in_stress.rs exists, is not #[ignore], and loops on writer and forker threads. budgets.rs:21-129 computes the producer row as the maximum over capabilities and gives the "update docs/system-facts.md" message the plan relies on. The planner row is contract plus planner frame only, so it does not move. I counted the guidance paragraph at 449 bytes, which matches the plan. The plan also has a cut order in case the measured set is above 1195. The forced one-number edit to docs/system-facts.md is justified by code and disclosed. The new test fails on the base tree, through its first expect, and it pins every element, including the report clause. No refusal rule is added. The dependents I grepped (the context headroom tests, run_pin_tests' own copy, the xtask compiled_in_files scan, refusal_corpus' CHANGELOG reads, the decision-log rules) are covered. All remaining findings are minor or nit: the change description should name the root cause explicitly, the shell-program check is a denylist, the design-stage gap is deferred, and the paragraph-order pin is rigid.
